Self-treatment of basal cell carcinoma on the nasal tip by a 51-year-old man using a top- ical caustic preparation containing Sanguinaria canadensis has been reported.1 Although a similar caustic paste was originally used in the 1930s as part of Mohs’ micrographic surgery (MMS) for some types of skin cancer, the MMS technique in use today is more refined, and self-administration of caustic pastes contain- ing sanguinaria for skin lesions is not recommended. 1. Profile Sapropterin, the active form of tetrahydrobiopterin, is used as the hydrochloride for the diagnosis and treatment of variant forms of phenylketonuria (hyperphenylalaninaemia, p.1922) associated with tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiency. It is given by mouth in daily doses of 1 to 20 mg/kg, in 2 or more divided doses
